front: A frota de Pedro Álvares Cabral chegou ao litoral da Bahia em 1500.
pronunciation: ah FROH-tah jee PEH-droo AHL-vah-reez kah-BRAHL sheh-GOH ah-oo lee-toh-RAHL dah bah-EE-ah eng MEEL ee kee-NYEHN-toos.
back: Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet reached the coast of Bahia in 1500.
context: Many historians prefer 'chegada' (arrival) to 'descobrimento' (discovery), since Indigenous peoples already lived there.

front: O país recebeu o nome de uma árvore, o pau-brasil, explorada pelos portugueses.
pronunciation: oo pah-EES rreh-seh-BEH-oo oo NOH-mee jee OO-mah AHR-voh-ree, oo pow-brah-ZEE-oo, ehs-ploh-RAH-dah PEH-looz pohr-too-GEH-zees.
back: The country was named after a tree, brazilwood, exploited by the Portuguese.
context: Brazilwood produced a red dye; 'brasa' means ember. 'Explorar' = to exploit (resources) or explore.

front: As capitanias hereditárias dividiram o território em faixas doadas a nobres.
pronunciation: ahs kah-pee-tah-NEE-ahz eh-reh-jee-TAH-ryahz jee-vee-JEE-rowng oo teh-rree-TOH-ryoo eng FAHY-shahz doh-AH-dahz ah NOH-brees.
back: The hereditary captaincies divided the territory into strips granted to noblemen.
context: First colonial administrative system (1530s). 'Faixa' = strip, band.

front: O ciclo do açúcar dependeu brutalmente da mão de obra escravizada.
pronunciation: oo SEE-kloo doo ah-SOO-kahr deh-pehn-DEH-oo broo-tah-oo-MEHN-chee dah MOWNG jee OH-brah ehs-krah-vee-ZAH-dah.
back: The sugar cycle depended brutally on enslaved labor.
context: Today 'escravizado' (enslaved) is preferred to 'escravo' (slave), stressing that slavery was imposed. 'Mão de obra' = labor force.

front: Palmares foi o maior quilombo do período colonial.
pronunciation: pah-oo-MAH-reez FOY oo mah-YOHR kee-LOHM-boo doo peh-REE-oh-doo koh-loh-nee-OW.
back: Palmares was the largest quilombo of the colonial period.
context: 'Quilombo' = community founded by people who escaped slavery. Its leader Zumbi died on November 20, now Black Consciousness Day.

front: A descoberta de ouro em Minas Gerais deslocou o eixo econômico da colônia.
pronunciation: ah jehs-koh-BEHR-tah jee OH-roo eng MEE-nahz zheh-RAHYZ jehz-loh-KOH oo AY-shoo eh-koh-NOH-mee-koo dah koh-LOH-nyah.
back: The discovery of gold in Minas Gerais shifted the colony's economic center.
context: The 18th-century gold cycle moved the capital from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro in 1763. 'Eixo' = axis.

front: As igrejas de Ouro Preto são joias do barroco mineiro.
pronunciation: ahz ee-GREH-zhahz jee OH-roo PREH-too SOWNG ZHOY-ahz doo bah-RROH-koo mee-NAY-roo.
back: The churches of Ouro Preto are gems of the Minas Gerais Baroque.
context: 'Barroco mineiro' is a distinctive local Baroque, financed by gold. Ouro Preto is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

front: Aleijadinho esculpiu os doze profetas de Congonhas em pedra-sabão.
pronunciation: ah-lay-zhah-JEE-nyoo ehs-kool-PEE-oo ooz DOH-zee proh-FEH-tahz jee kohn-GOH-nyahz eng PEH-drah-sah-BOWNG.
back: Aleijadinho sculpted the twelve prophets of Congonhas in soapstone.
context: Antônio Francisco Lisboa, 'Aleijadinho' ('little cripple'), kept working despite a degenerative illness.

front: Tiradentes foi enforcado em 1792 e virou símbolo da Inconfidência Mineira.
pronunciation: chee-rah-DEHN-cheez FOY ehn-fohr-KAH-doo eng MEEL seh-teh-SEHN-tooz ee noh-VEHN-tah ee DOYS ee vee-ROH SEEM-boh-loo dah een-kohn-fee-DEHN-syah mee-NAY-rah.
back: Tiradentes was hanged in 1792 and became the symbol of the Minas Conspiracy.
context: The Inconfidência Mineira was a conspiracy against Portuguese taxes on gold. April 21 is a national holiday in his honor.

front: Em 1808, a corte portuguesa fugiu de Napoleão e se instalou no Rio de Janeiro.
pronunciation: eng MEEL oy-toh-SEHN-tooz ee OY-too, ah KOHR-chee pohr-too-GEH-zah foo-ZHEE-oo jee nah-poh-leh-OWNG ee see eens-tah-LOH noo RREE-oo jee zhah-NAY-roo.
back: In 1808, the Portuguese court fled Napoleon and settled in Rio de Janeiro.
context: A unique event: a European capital moved to its colony. It opened the ports and transformed Rio.

front: Dom Pedro proclamou a independência às margens do rio Ipiranga.
pronunciation: DOHNG PEH-droo proh-klah-MOH ah een-deh-pehn-DEHN-syah AHZ MAHR-zhengz doo RREE-oo ee-pee-RAHN-gah.
back: Dom Pedro proclaimed independence on the banks of the Ipiranga River.
context: September 7, 1822. The 'Grito do Ipiranga' ('Independência ou morte!') opens the national anthem: 'Ouviram do Ipiranga as margens plácidas'.

front: Diferentemente dos vizinhos, o Brasil se tornou um império, e não uma república.
pronunciation: jee-feh-rehn-cheh-MEHN-chee dooz vee-ZEE-nyooz, oo brah-ZEE-oo see tohr-NOH oong eem-PEH-ryoo, ee NOWNG OO-mah rreh-POO-blee-kah.
back: Unlike its neighbors, Brazil became an empire, not a republic.
context: 'Diferentemente de' = unlike. The Empire lasted from 1822 to 1889 under Pedro I and Pedro II.

front: Dom Pedro II governou por quase cinquenta anos e era apaixonado por ciência.
pronunciation: DOHNG PEH-droo seh-GOON-doo goh-vehr-NOH pohr KWAH-zee seen-KWEHN-tah AH-nooz ee EH-rah ah-pahy-shoh-NAH-doo pohr see-EHN-syah.
back: Dom Pedro II ruled for almost fifty years and was passionate about science.
context: Roman numerals are read as ordinals up to ten: 'Pedro Segundo'. 'Apaixonado por' = passionate about.

front: A Lei Áurea, assinada pela princesa Isabel em 1888, aboliu a escravidão.
pronunciation: ah LAY OW-ree-ah, ah-see-NAH-dah PEH-lah preen-SEH-zah ee-zah-BEH-oo eng MEEL oy-toh-SEHN-tooz ee oy-TEHN-tah ee OY-too, ah-boh-LEE-oo ah ehs-krah-vee-DOWNG.
back: The Golden Law, signed by Princess Isabel in 1888, abolished slavery.
context: Signed on May 13, 1888. Brazil was the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery, with no compensation or integration for the freed.

front: O fim da escravidão sem políticas de inclusão deixou marcas que persistem até hoje.
pronunciation: oo FEENG dah ehs-krah-vee-DOWNG seng poh-LEE-chee-kahz jee een-kloo-ZOWNG day-SHOH MAHR-kahs keh pehr-SEES-teng ah-TEH OH-zhee.
back: The end of slavery without inclusion policies left scars that persist to this day.
context: A frequent theme in Brazilian debates on structural racism. 'Deixar marcas' = to leave scars.

front: A República foi proclamada em 15 de novembro de 1889 por um golpe militar.
pronunciation: ah rreh-POO-blee-kah FOY proh-klah-MAH-dah eng KEEN-zee jee noh-VEHM-broo jee MEEL oy-toh-SEHN-tooz ee oy-TEHN-tah ee NOH-vee pohr oong GOHL-pee mee-lee-TAHR.
back: The Republic was proclaimed on November 15, 1889, by a military coup.
context: Led by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca. The emperor and his family went into exile in Europe.

front: Na República Velha, São Paulo e Minas alternavam o poder na política do café com leite.
pronunciation: nah rreh-POO-blee-kah VEH-lyah, SOWNG POW-loo ee MEE-nahz ahl-tehr-NAH-vowng oo poh-DEHR nah poh-LEE-chee-kah doo kah-FEH kohng LAY-chee.
back: In the Old Republic, São Paulo and Minas took turns in power under the 'coffee with milk' politics.
context: São Paulo produced coffee and Minas Gerais was known for dairy. The arrangement ended with the 1930 Revolution.

front: O voto era aberto, e os coronéis controlavam os eleitores com o voto de cabresto.
pronunciation: oo VOH-too EH-rah ah-BEHR-too, ee ooz koh-roh-NEHYS kohn-troh-LAH-vowng ooz eh-lay-TOH-rees kohng oo VOH-too jee kah-BREHS-too.
back: Voting was public, and local bosses controlled voters through the 'halter vote'.
context: 'Coronelismo': rural landowners ('coronéis') dictated votes. 'Cabresto' = halter, as in leading a horse.

front: A Revolução de 1930 levou Getúlio Vargas ao poder.
pronunciation: ah rreh-voh-loo-SOWNG jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee TREEN-tah leh-VOH zheh-TOO-lyoo VAHR-gahz ah-oo poh-DEHR.
back: The 1930 Revolution brought Getúlio Vargas to power.
context: Vargas dominated Brazilian politics until 1954. 'Levar ao poder' = to bring to power.

front: Durante o Estado Novo, Vargas fechou o Congresso e censurou a imprensa.
pronunciation: doo-RAHN-chee oo ehs-TAH-doo NOH-voo, VAHR-gahs feh-SHOH oo kohn-GREH-soo ee sehn-soo-ROH ah eem-PREHN-sah.
back: During the Estado Novo, Vargas shut down Congress and censored the press.
context: The Estado Novo (1937–1945) was an authoritarian regime. 'Imprensa' = the press.

front: A CLT, criada em 1943, ainda rege as relações de trabalho no país.
pronunciation: ah seh-EH-lee-TEH, kree-AH-dah eng MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee kwah-REHN-tah ee TREHS, ah-EEN-dah RREH-zhee ahs rreh-lah-SOYNGZ jee trah-BAH-lyoo noo pah-EES.
back: The CLT, created in 1943, still governs labor relations in the country.
context: The Consolidation of Labor Laws brought the minimum wage, paid vacation and the 'carteira de trabalho'. 'Reger' = to govern.

front: Saio da vida para entrar na história.
pronunciation: SAHY-oo dah VEE-dah PAH-rah ehn-TRAHR nah ees-TOH-ryah.
back: I leave life to enter history.
context: Final line of Vargas's suicide letter (August 1954), one of the most famous sentences in Brazilian politics.

front: Juscelino Kubitschek prometeu cinquenta anos de progresso em cinco.
pronunciation: zhoo-seh-LEE-noo koo-bee-CHEH-kee proh-meh-TEH-oo seen-KWEHN-tah AH-nooz jee proh-GREH-soo eng SEEN-koo.
back: Juscelino Kubitschek promised fifty years of progress in five.
context: JK's slogan '50 anos em 5' (1956–1961). His era is remembered for optimism, industry and bossa nova.

front: Brasília foi inaugurada em 1960 e projetada por Lúcio Costa e Oscar Niemeyer.
pronunciation: brah-ZEE-lyah FOY ee-now-goo-RAH-dah eng MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee seh-SEHN-tah ee proh-zheh-TAH-dah pohr LOO-syoo KOHS-tah ee ohs-KAHR nee-eh-MAY-ehr.
back: Brasília was inaugurated in 1960 and designed by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer.
context: Built in about four years in the middle of the Cerrado. Costa drew the urban plan; Niemeyer, the buildings.

front: O golpe de 1964 instaurou uma ditadura militar que durou vinte e um anos.
pronunciation: oo GOHL-pee jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee seh-SEHN-tah ee KWAH-troo eens-tow-ROH OO-mah jee-tah-DOO-rah mee-lee-TAHR keh doo-ROH VEEN-chee ee OONG AH-noos.
back: The 1964 coup established a military dictatorship that lasted twenty-one years.
context: 'Golpe' = coup. 'Instaurar' = to establish (a regime). The dictatorship lasted from 1964 to 1985.

front: O AI-5, de 1968, endureceu o regime e suspendeu direitos fundamentais.
pronunciation: oo AH-ee SEEN-koo, jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee seh-SEHN-tah ee OY-too, ehn-doo-reh-SEH-oo oo rreh-ZHEE-mee ee soos-pehn-DEH-oo jee-RAY-toos foon-dah-mehn-TAHYS.
back: AI-5, from 1968, hardened the regime and suspended fundamental rights.
context: Institutional Act No. 5 closed Congress and suspended habeas corpus for political crimes, opening the 'anos de chumbo'.

front: Os anos de chumbo foram marcados por censura, tortura e desaparecimentos.
pronunciation: ooz AH-nooz jee SHOOM-boo FOH-rowng mahr-KAH-doos pohr sehn-SOO-rah, tohr-TOO-rah ee jee-zah-pah-reh-see-MEHN-toos.
back: The 'years of lead' were marked by censorship, torture and disappearances.
context: 'Anos de chumbo' (years of lead) = the most repressive phase, roughly 1968–1974. 'Ser marcado por' = to be marked by.

front: Muitos artistas e intelectuais foram para o exílio.
pronunciation: MOOY-tooz ahr-CHEES-tahz ee een-teh-lehk-too-AHYS FOH-rowng PAH-rah oo eh-ZEE-lyoo.
back: Many artists and intellectuals went into exile.
context: Among them Caetano Veloso, Gilberto Gil and Chico Buarque. 'Ir para o exílio' = to go into exile.

front: A Lei da Anistia de 1979 permitiu a volta dos exilados.
pronunciation: ah LAY dah ah-nees-CHEE-ah jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee seh-TEHN-tah ee NOH-vee pehr-mee-CHEE-oo ah VOHL-tah dooz eh-zee-LAH-doos.
back: The 1979 Amnesty Law allowed exiles to return.
context: It also protected agents of the regime, which remains a controversial issue.

front: O movimento Diretas Já levou milhões às ruas pelo voto direto para presidente.
pronunciation: oo moh-vee-MEHN-too jee-REH-tahz ZHAH leh-VOH mee-LYOYNGZ AHS RROO-ahs PEH-loo VOH-too jee-REH-too PAH-rah preh-zee-DEHN-chee.
back: The Direct Elections Now movement brought millions onto the streets for the direct presidential vote.
context: 1983–1984. The amendment failed in Congress, but the movement accelerated the end of the regime.

front: Tancredo Neves foi eleito indiretamente, mas morreu antes de tomar posse.
pronunciation: tahn-KREH-doo NEH-veez FOY eh-LAY-too een-jee-reh-tah-MEHN-chee, mahz moh-RREH-oo AHN-cheez jee toh-MAHR POH-see.
back: Tancredo Neves was elected indirectly, but died before taking office.
context: 1985: his vice-president, José Sarney, became the first civilian president after the dictatorship. 'Tomar posse' = to take office.

front: A Constituição de 1988 ficou conhecida como Constituição Cidadã.
pronunciation: ah kohns-chee-too-ee-SOWNG jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee oy-TEHN-tah ee OY-too fee-KOH koh-nyeh-SEE-dah KOH-moo kohns-chee-too-ee-SOWNG see-dah-DOWNG.
back: The 1988 Constitution became known as the Citizen Constitution.
context: Named by Ulysses Guimarães for its broad social rights, including the universal health system (SUS).

front: A redemocratização trouxe de volta as eleições diretas em 1989.
pronunciation: ah rreh-deh-moh-krah-chee-zah-SOWNG TROH-see jee VOHL-tah ahz eh-lay-SOYNGZ jee-REH-tahz eng MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee oy-TEHN-tah ee NOH-vee.
back: Redemocratization brought back direct elections in 1989.
context: 'Trazer de volta' = to bring back. Fernando Collor won the first direct presidential election since 1960.

front: Collor sofreu impeachment em 1992 após denúncias de corrupção.
pronunciation: KOH-lohr soh-FREH-oo eem-PEECH-mehn-chee eng MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee noh-VEHN-tah ee DOYS ah-POHZ deh-NOON-syahz jee koh-rroop-SOWNG.
back: Collor was impeached in 1992 after corruption allegations.
context: He resigned before the final vote. Students with painted faces ('caras-pintadas') protested on the streets. 'Denúncia' = allegation, accusation.

front: O Plano Real de 1994 finalmente controlou a hiperinflação.
pronunciation: oo PLAH-noo rreh-AHL jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee noh-VEHN-tah ee KWAH-troo fee-nah-oo-MEHN-chee kohn-troh-LOH ah ee-pehr-een-flah-SOWNG.
back: The 1994 Real Plan finally brought hyperinflation under control.
context: Before it, prices could change daily. The plan created the current currency, the real.

front: Quem viveu a hiperinflação lembra das remarcações de preço todos os dias.
pronunciation: KENG vee-VEH-oo ah ee-pehr-een-flah-SOWNG LEHM-brah dahz rreh-mahr-kah-SOYNGZ jee PREH-soo TOH-dooz ooz JEE-ahs.
back: Anyone who lived through hyperinflation remembers prices being re-marked every day.
context: Supermarket staff relabeled goods with price guns, sometimes several times a day.

front: Esse período é estudado de forma diferente dependendo da corrente historiográfica.
pronunciation: EH-see peh-REE-oh-doo EH ehs-too-DAH-doo jee FOHR-mah jee-feh-REHN-chee deh-pehn-DEHN-doo dah koh-RREHN-chee ees-toh-ryoh-GRAH-fee-kah.
back: That period is studied differently depending on the historiographical school.
context: 'Corrente' = current, school of thought. Useful for nuanced academic discussion.

front: A memória da ditadura ainda divide a sociedade brasileira.
pronunciation: ah meh-MOH-ryah dah jee-tah-DOO-rah ah-EEN-dah jee-VEE-jee ah soh-syeh-DAH-jee brah-zee-LAY-rah.
back: The memory of the dictatorship still divides Brazilian society.
context: The National Truth Commission (2012–2014) investigated crimes of the period.

front: O Brasil recebeu milhões de imigrantes italianos, japoneses e alemães.
pronunciation: oo brah-ZEE-oo rreh-seh-BEH-oo mee-LYOYNGZ jee ee-mee-GRAHN-cheez ee-tah-lee-AH-nooz, zhah-poh-NEH-zeez ee ah-leh-MAYNGS.
back: Brazil received millions of Italian, Japanese and German immigrants.
context: From the late 19th century; São Paulo has the largest Japanese community outside Japan. 'Alemães' = plural of 'alemão'.

front: A Revolução Farroupilha foi a mais longa revolta do período imperial.
pronunciation: ah rreh-voh-loo-SOWNG fah-rroh-PEE-lyah FOY ah MAHYZ LOHN-gah rreh-VOHL-tah doo peh-REE-oh-doo eem-peh-ree-OW.
back: The Ragamuffin War was the longest revolt of the imperial period.
context: 1835–1845 in Rio Grande do Sul. Its legacy remains central to gaúcho identity.

front: Canudos resistiu a várias expedições do exército antes de ser destruído.
pronunciation: kah-NOO-dooz rreh-zees-CHEE-oo ah VAH-ryahz ehs-peh-jee-SOYNGZ doo eh-ZEHR-see-too AHN-cheez jee SEHR dehs-troo-EE-doo.
back: Canudos resisted several army expeditions before being destroyed.
context: 1896–1897 in the Bahia backlands, led by Antônio Conselheiro. Narrated by Euclides da Cunha in 'Os Sertões'.

front: A Era Vargas deixou um legado ambíguo: direitos trabalhistas e autoritarismo.
pronunciation: ah EH-rah VAHR-gahz day-SHOH oong leh-GAH-doo ahm-BEE-gwoo: jee-RAY-toos trah-bah-LYEES-tahz ee ow-toh-ree-tah-REEZ-moo.
back: The Vargas Era left an ambiguous legacy: labor rights and authoritarianism.
context: 'Legado' = legacy. A balanced sentence typical of history essays.

front: Para entender o Brasil atual, é preciso conhecer a herança colonial.
pronunciation: PAH-rah ehn-tehn-DEHR oo brah-ZEE-oo ah-too-AHL, EH preh-SEE-zoo koh-nyeh-SEHR ah eh-RAHN-sah koh-loh-nee-OW.
back: To understand today's Brazil, you need to know its colonial legacy.
context: 'Herança' = inheritance, legacy. 'Atual' = current (not 'actual').

front: Os historiadores divergem quanto às causas do declínio do Império.
pronunciation: ooz ees-toh-ryah-DOH-reez jee-VEHR-zheng KWAHN-too AHS KOW-zahz doo deh-KLEE-nyoo doo eem-PEH-ryoo.
back: Historians disagree about the causes of the Empire's decline.
context: 'Divergir quanto a' = to disagree regarding. Note the crase: 'quanto às causas'.

front: Ouviram do Ipiranga as margens plácidas de um povo heroico o brado retumbante.
pronunciation: oh-VEE-rowng doo ee-pee-RAHN-gah ahz MAHR-zhengs PLAH-see-dahz jee oong POH-voo eh-ROY-koo oo BRAH-doo rreh-toom-BAHN-chee.
back: The placid banks of the Ipiranga heard the resounding cry of a heroic people.
context: Opening lines of the national anthem, famous for its inverted word order: the subject ('as margens plácidas') comes after the verb.
